verdict.rationale: The docs say Trigger.dev lets you write workflows in plain async TypeScript with checkpoint-resume durability, and that triggering a task returns a handle you can use to check status, cancel, or retry. That loosely implies tasks can be composed in code without hand-rolled coordination, but nothing in the pack shows parallel steps, batch fan-out/fan-in, or child-task waits. Missing for 10: documented parallel step execution, dynamic batch fan-out with fan-in result aggregation, child task trigger-and-wait semantics, independent hands-on corroboration.
